page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained core configuration. It is built on the AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture, delivering a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Alongside compute resources, the instance includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing an elevated allocation of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, as well as a 322 GB local SSD temporary disk.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-threaded execution paired with moderate overall throughput due to the constrained core count. The instance achieves a strong rating in stress-ng single-core CPU testing (2702.28) and an average Geekbench single-core score of 1592.0. Large-block uncached read memory bandwidth holds an average rating at 39.33 GB/sec, matching average results in PassMark memory testing (2462.52) and gzip single-threaded compression (25.73 GB/sec). However, multi-core metrics reflect the limited 4-vCPU envelope, registering in the lower quartile for multi-core stress-ng (5399.28), multi-core Geekbench (3646.0), and aggregate PassMark CPU benchmarks (6181.49).

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the constrained vCPU layout optimizes software licensing and resource utilization. Workloads that demand substantial memory footprints but limited parallel compute threads can run economically without paying for unnecessary compute capacity. The inclusion of 322 GB of local SSD provides fast scratch space, though workloads requiring sustained concurrent multi-threading may face bottlenecks under heavy load. The E8-4ads_v5 is best suited for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caching platforms, and data processing tasks requiring high RAM per thread.
